Resolves #18846

Rows the Navigator skips (disabled rows, separators) no longer break its two "last row" and "press" contracts:
- **End** takes the last match of the navigable selector. Before, it used `:last-of-type`, which matched nothing when the last row was not navigable. The previous-key wrap fallback shares the lookup, and `navigateGetAdjacent`'s unreachable wrap branch is deleted.
- **A press on no navigable item** keeps focus where it is, as `navigateMouseDownHandler` already did for items without a focusable. Before, a click on a disabled row or a separator blurred the active item to the body, and a floating menu dismissed itself on the focus leave.
- **A press on the subject's own scrollbar** keeps its default.

Evidence: L2 (component tier, headless Chromium, real pointer + keys) → L2 required (every AC of #18846 is a component-tier behaviour). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `component/menu/List.spec.mjs` › *End lands on the last interactive row when the last row is disabled* / *…is a separator*. Red first on `dev`'s Navigator (below) |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: › *CONTROL: End reaches an interactive last row, and Home passes over a disabled first row*. Green on `dev` too, as a control should be |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: › *a press on a disabled row keeps the menu open, with focus where it was* / *…on a separator*. Red first on `dev` |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: the CONTROL half of the AC-3 arms (clicking the interactive `Gamma` still activates and closes the menu), and › *CONTROL: after a press on a disabled row, a press outside the menu still dismisses it* |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: › *an embedded menu keeps focus on its active item when a press lands on a disabled row* (red first on `dev`) and › *a press outside the menu's client area, where its scrollbar lies, keeps its default*. Outside-CI: a real scrollbar drag, below |
| AC-6 | the arms sit in `test/playwright/component/menu/List.spec.mjs`, in a new `rows the Navigator skips` describe beside the keyboard cascade |

## Deltas from ticket

- The scrollbar AC produced a small guard, `isScrollbarPress()`, rather than only a test. Headless Chromium draws no scrollbars, so the arm stands a 16 px right border in for one: both lie outside the client area.

## Test Evidence

- **Red first.** `dev`'s `src/main/addon/Navigator.mjs` swapped in: 6 of 7 new arms fail and the CONTROL passes. Restored: 7/7. With the outside-press control added, the menu component spec passes 28/28. The full component suite gave 336 passed and 1 failed. The failure was `dashboard/DockRailRevealIframe.spec.mjs:221`, a raw-pointer drag from a plain span, with no Navigator subject involved. It passes 3/3 alone on this branch and 3/3 with `dev`'s Navigator.
- **Mutation.** Dropping `&& !this.isScrollbarPress(e, data.subject)` turns the client-area arm red (`outside: true`).
- **Real scrollbar drag,** in the in-app browser (headed Chromium, macOS overlay scrollbars), on an embedded 31-row menu. With the overlay thumb visible, the press targets the list *inside* its client area (`offsetX 235 < clientWidth 238`), so the new rule prevents its default (`defaultPrevented: true`). The drag still scrolls (`scrollTop` 100 → 563), and focus stays on the active row. Chromium does not let a cancelled `mousedown` stop a scrollbar drag. The guard keeps the classic-scrollbar case correct by construction in browsers I could not measure.
- **Not exercised by any arm:** the carve-out that lets a focusable element inside the subject but outside every item still take focus. No in-tree list renders one.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — the carve-out's blast radius is wider than the body states, and it is the subject that decides it.**

The body says: *"Not exercised by any arm: the carve-out that lets a focusable element inside the subject but outside every item still take focus. No in-tree list renders one."* That is true, and it understates the dependency. `DomUtils.closest(el, filterFn, limit)` walks `while (el?.nodeType === ELEMENT_NODE && el !== limit)` **starting at `el`**, and in exactly the case this branch exists for — a press on a disabled row or a separator, which take no pointer events — `e.target` **is** `data.subject`. So the subject is the first node tested, and the limit only excludes `subject.parentNode`.

Consequence: a list whose **root** is focusable does not lose the carve-out for presses on that root. It loses the entire dead-space rule, for every press, silently — `closest` returns the subject on the first iteration and `preventDefault()` never runs.

I checked whether that is reachable and it is not, today:

- `isFocusable(e)` is `isTabbable(e) || Number(e.getAttribute('tabIndex')) < 0`, and `Number(null)` is `0`, so an absent attribute is correctly not focusable.
- The only in-tree `tabIndex: -1` assignments on this path are `list/Chip.mjs:95` and `list/Circle.mjs:75`, both inside `Neo.create({parentId: me.id, …})` — **items**, not roots — and `list/Base.mjs:527` is likewise `item.tabIndex = -1`. `menu/List.mjs:422` deletes item tabIndex outright. No list root carries one.

So this is latent, not live, and I am not asking for a guard. What I would ask for is one clause in the `navigateMouseDownHandler` comment saying the walk starts at the subject, so the next person who makes a list root focusable meets the dependency where they can violate it rather than in a bug report. Your call — it is a comment, and you own the file.

**Non-blocking, second:** the picker fields are named in the ticket's Architectural Reality as consumers whose behaviour changes (*"there the dead-space press currently takes focus out of the field"*), and no arm covers one. The embedded-menu arm stands in for `list.Base` and satisfies AC-5 as written, so this is not an AC gap. It is the *interesting* case that goes unwitnessed: for a ComboBox the focus lives on an input **outside** the subject, so what makes the fix work there is precisely that `closest`'s limit is `subject.parentNode` and the walk can never reach the input. That is the one consumer where the cap's value is load-bearing, and it is the one with no arm.

**What I pushed on and could not break:**

- **The deleted wrap branch.** I did not need the TreeWalker invariant to clear it: `querySelector` returns `Element | null`, so `allItems[direction === 1 ? 0 : allItems.length - 1]` could only ever evaluate to `undefined` — or **throw** on `null[0]` when nothing matched. Falling through returns `undefined` too, so the removal is behaviour-preserving where the branch was reachable and removes a latent `TypeError` where it was not. Strictly safer, not merely equivalent.
- **`navigateGetAdjacent`'s restructure.** Old outer `if (treeWalker.currentNode)` was always true (`currentNode` is initialised to the assigned node and `nextNode()` leaves it in place when it finds nothing), so `if (currentNode !== data.activeItem) return currentNode` is the same predicate with one fewer level. Same undefined on the no-move path.
- **An inner scroller inside the subject** would make `target === scroller` false and break a scrollbar drag. It does not occur: the scroll is on `.neo-list` / `.neo-menu-list` itself, which is the subject, and `.neo-list-wrapper`'s `overflow: hidden` is an ancestor the subject-bound listener never hears from anyway.
- **`Array.from(...).at(-1)`** rather than `.at(-1)` on the NodeList directly — necessary, `NodeList` has no `at()`.

**Rhetorical-Drift Audit (per guide §7.4):**

- [x] PR description: framing matches the diff
- [x] Anchor & Echo summaries: `navigateGetLast`'s docblock states *why* `:last-of-type` cannot express the intent, which is the defect itself rather than a restatement of the method name
- [x] `[RETROSPECTIVE]` tag: N/A — none carried
- [x] Linked anchors: `00a67f1020` (#5123) does carry the `:last-of-type` line

**Findings:** Pass, and better than pass on one axis. The body publishes a result that argues *against* its own scrollbar story — on macOS overlay scrollbars the press lands **inside** the client area (`offsetX 235 < clientWidth 238`), so the new guard does not fire at all and the drag scrolls only because Chromium ignores a cancelled `mousedown` for scrollbar drags. Reporting that the measurement did not exercise the guard, instead of reporting "scrollbar drag verified", is the opposite of drift.
